title: Route Machines on Machines in the shared Cyclotron (r5 cutover)
description:
Machines on Machines (AnthusAI/Machines-on-Machines) replaces read.p.apyr.us as its own Papyrus site; the p-apyr-us corpus and knowledge base move there, and read.p.apyr.us redirects. Papyrus implementation builds the site; Cyclotron's part is the scoring and routing.

Prepared: #185 (develop) renames p-apyr-us-relevance to 'Machines on Machines relevance' at revision 3 and defines shared-source-relevance-r5; infra/lab/criteria-runbook.md section r5. Ryan chose to apply it in the same cutover as the new site, so the six bindings and the router move once.

Open before applying:
- The handoff (docs/handoff.md) says the doctrine will be rewritten for a broader AI/ML mission. #185 kept the old mission (Ryan, 2026-11-01). If the new doctrine is approved before the cutover, rewrite the revision 3 question from it and get Ryan's approval of the text.
- Binding id: the site id / corpus key (suggested machines-on-machines). The binding keeps output p-apyr-us-relevance and priming list prime-p-apyr-us.
- Whether the p-apyr-us binding is retired (p.apyr.us stays the Papyrus marketing site).

Acceptance:
- plan shows save only for p-apyr-us-relevance and define r5, no drift; Ryan approves each write step.
- Successor run bootstrapped; StandingRuns change set reviewed and executed; bindings at revision 5 with the new binding id.
- prime-p-apyr-us relabelled under revision 3 and primed; every other binding primed on the new run.
- Papyrus router CONFIG#router points at the new run and binding revision 5 with the new publication; a dry-run sweep, then live; first receipts show bindingRevision 5 and the Machines on Machines classifier.

comments.author: home
comments.text: r5 repair 2026-11-02, approved by Ryan in this session. Cause: all ledgers share one replies lake (replies-ledger, about 8,150 records); a new ledger's first settle steps past each one at about 110 ms and hit the 900s worker limit. Job ae9d38b9 (hn-50312408) timed out, leaving its running claim and 7 engine records owned by the dead invocation (7cfb79aa). Repair from a Mac: released the 7 owners, set the new ledger's coverage to last 8154 with 1..8153 skipped (seq 8154 is a foreign record it vouches for but never cites), reconciled ae9d38b9 as failed with command_recovery, woke the queue. Prior heads saved locally. Result: the other 9 queued jobs completed in about 50s. Open: the provider call for hn-50312408 may have been paid and needs an operator retry; the shared lake is not fixed in code, so any next new run repeats this.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Second repair 2026-11-02, approved by Ryan in this session. The router re-posted hn-50312408 as job ab42589a; it raised BatchInProgress on the orphaned, claimed shared request, which leaves a job running with its claim held and blocks the queue. Closed that request as interrupted/abandoned (fingerprint f94d187f), knowingly allowing one repeat model call despite the guard against repaying claimed requests, then reconciled ab42589a as failed and woke the queue. The 3 jobs behind it completed. Code fix list: per-ledger replies lake; BatchInProgress must end a job terminally; a worker timeout must not leave a claimed request needing a hand edit.
